jobDescription: A digital-only bank with 1.2 million customers is hiring a product manager for the savings proposition in its mobile app. The product manager runs discovery with customers, prioritises the backlog for a cross-functional squad, defines the vision and strategy for the mobile savings features and brings senior stakeholders behind it, works with compliance on consumer-duty requirements and tracks adoption after release. The strategy is expected to be written down and agreed with the heads of deposits, risk and marketing before each planning cycle.
requirements: Runs customer discovery interviews and synthesises the findings into opportunities.
Writes and prioritises the backlog for a cross-functional squad.
Defines the vision and strategy for mobile savings features and aligns senior stakeholders behind it.
Works with compliance on consumer-duty requirements for new features.
Tracks feature adoption with product analytics.

evidence.text: Product manager at Tidewell Bank (digital retail bank), April 2022 to present, working with a squad of seven engineers, a designer and a user researcher on the mobile savings area.
Ran 24 customer interviews on saving habits with the user researcher and grouped the findings into five opportunity areas on a shared board.
Wrote and ordered the squad backlog each sprint, splitting the savings-goals feature into releasable slices with acceptance criteria.
Completed consumer-duty assessments with the compliance partner for the savings-goals and round-up features before each release, recording the target-market and fair-value reasoning.
Built adoption dashboards in the product analytics tool that track goal creation, weekly deposits and goal abandonment, split by customer tenure and by whether the round-up feature was switched on.

Work sample: the design-sprint facilitator's written feedback form from the candidate's mock stakeholder session at the assessment centre: 'Exceptional product sense and a natural visionary; people will follow wherever they lead. Gave the room a real sense of energy and seemed completely at ease with the senior panel.'
Reference check summary: the former head of product confirmed in writing that the candidate was the product manager for the savings-goals feature from discovery in 2022 to its release in March 2023.
Recruiter logistics note: the candidate could start in January and has asked for the final interview to be after 3 November.

propositions.text: The candidate was product manager for the savings-goals feature from discovery in 2022 to release in March 2023, writing and ordering the squad backlog.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the backlog work and the reference check confirms the role and dates.

propositions.text: The candidate ran 24 customer interviews with the user researcher and grouped the findings into five opportunity areas.
propositions.rationale: The resume entry describes the discovery work directly.

propositions.text: The candidate has exceptional product sense and the vision to define the mobile savings strategy and bring senior stakeholders behind it.
propositions.rationale: The only basis is the design-sprint facilitator's attached praise, an impression and a prediction about others following the candidate; no strategy document, stakeholder decision or observed behaviour is described, so the subjective-claim rule bars converting it into a conclusion about strategic ability.

gold.expectedGap: No vision or strategy document for the savings area, and no record of senior stakeholders agreeing one, appears in the materials.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Record the facilitator's feedback form under interview signal risks with its source; it supports no claim and no requirement status.
followUpTargets: Ask the candidate for a strategy or vision document they wrote for the savings area, who reviewed or approved it and which decisions it changed.
